title: STUDY TOPIC Spiritual formation [the process of becoming like Jesus] part 1
devotional:
As we begin to look at spiritual formation, we need to start at the right place, we need to try and understand God’s original intention. Very often when it comes to understanding who we are, and the reason for our existence we start at the wrong place. Often we view mankind through the lens of sin. We have what I would call a ‘sin filter,’ So we view people primarily as ’sinners’ who need salvation. Now all that is absolutely true. However, if we make sin the starting point by which we are going to understand others or ourselves, then we are going to misunderstand what it means to be a person. We will be unable to grasp the wholeness that spiritual formation can bring. The best way for us to honestly recognise sin in our lives is to realise that sin should not define us. Imagine you had a sickness or some kind of disability, would you like that to become the thing that defines you. Or would want to be seen as someone who was more than a ‘sickness,’ or a ‘disability?’

We need to start where the bible starts. We need to root our understanding of who we are in the creation story and use the definition it uses. When God created mankind on the sixth day of creation, he expressed his intention for His creation of mankind.

Genesis 1:26 reads: - ‘’Then God said, “Let us make human beings in our image, to be like us. They will reign over the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, the livestock, all the wild animals on the earth, and the small animals that scurry along the ground.” So God created human beings in his own image. In the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.

The phrase ‘image of God’ is the first description of man, it is the first defining statement of humanity. ‘Image of God’ expresses the essence, purpose and potential of our humanity. ‘Image of God,’ encapsulates God’s good desire for you as a person and God’s will for your life. This initial defining designation by God over the creation of man is ultimate in nature, it cannot be improved or bettered. Seeing ourselves as made in the Image of God is the cure for a bad self-image and self-loathing. God wants us to see ourselves and everyone else as people made in His image.
prayer: Father thank you that you you have always seen us much more than people who are defined by sin
